In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of NMBDs should be avoided if at all possible, and if they are used, they should be used with the utmost caution.
the use of a train-of-four ratio of 0.9 or more and a TOF ratio of 0·4 or more is a safe and reliable indicator of the absence of clinically significant residual neuromusucular blockade.
the use of a peripheral nerve stimulator should be considered mandatory in all patients receiving NBDs and that a train-of-four ratio of 0.9 or greater is required to allow extubation.

the new generation monitoring and reversal agents are safe, reliable and effective in the management of neuromauscular blockade.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a quantitative nerve stimulator (QNS) is a key component of the strategy for managing neu-muscular blockade, but it is not a panacea.
